results.term_definition: The ionosphere is a part of the atmosphere (above about 80 kilometers). It contains a high concentration of ions due to the high-energy part of the radiation the Earth receives from the Sun, which breaks the molecules into atoms, and then atoms into ions and electrons. The presence of the free electrons makes this region of the atmosphere a good conductor of electricity. As such, the ionosphere is able to reflect radio waves at certain wavelengths.
